subject: paediatrics
title: Prematurity, Low Birth Weight and Ballard Gestational Assessment

steps.tx: Any neonate born before thirty-seven completed weeks of gestation is classified as **preterm birth**. Stratification categorizes extremely preterm as under twenty-eight weeks, very preterm as twenty-eight to thirty-one weeks, moderate preterm as thirty-two to thirty-three weeks, and late preterm as thirty-four to thirty-six completed weeks. Late preterms account for seventy percent of all preterm births.
steps.say: Preterm birth is delivery before thirty-seven weeks, categorized from extremely to late preterm.

vis.alt: Neonatal definitions, gestational age classification and growth curves.

steps.tx: Birth weight definitions classify an infant weighing under twenty-five hundred grams as **low birth weight**. A birth weight under fifteen hundred grams defines very low birth weight, while a weight under one thousand grams defines extremely low birth weight. Low birth weight arises from two distinct physiological pathways: preterm delivery, intrauterine fetal growth restriction, or a combination of both.
steps.say: Low birth weight is under twenty-five hundred grams, encompassing both preterm and growth-restricted infants.

rows: Increased risk of hypothermia and hypoglycemia
High incidence of RDS, IVH, and NEC
Requires tertiary NICU care and ventilatory support

steps.tx: An infant whose birth weight falls below the tenth percentile for gestational age is classified as **small for gestational age**. While some small infants are constitutionally small and physiologically healthy, others suffer pathological intrauterine growth restriction resulting from maternal vascular disease, severe placental insufficiency, fetal chromosomal aneuploidy, or congenital intrauterine infections.
steps.say: Small for gestational age denotes weight below the tenth percentile, encompassing constitutionally small and growth-restricted infants.

left.title: SGA (Statistical Definition)
points: Based strictly on population growth standards

right.title: IUGR (Pathological Process)
points: Failure to achieve genetic growth potential
Associated with abnormal umbilical artery Doppler

steps.tx: Growth restriction is divided into symmetrical and asymmetrical patterns. In **asymmetrical growth restriction**, late uteroplacental insufficiency compromises liver glycogen storage and abdominal fat while preferentially sparing blood flow to the fetal brain. Consequently, the head circumference remains normal while abdominal circumference and birth weight are severely reduced, resulting in a low Ponderal index.
steps.say: Asymmetrical growth restriction spares the head while depleting liver glycogen and abdominal fat.

steps.tx: Accurate clinical estimation of gestational age within forty-eight hours of birth utilizes the **New Ballard score**. By assigning numerical values to six physical and six neurological criteria, the score accurately estimates gestational age between twenty and forty-four weeks within plus or minus two weeks, even in extremely premature neonates.
steps.say: The New Ballard score evaluates physical and neurological maturity to assess gestational age.

left.title: Physical Maturity Criteria
points: Plantar creases, breast bud, ear cartilage, genitalia

right.title: Neuromuscular Criteria
points: Resting posture and square window angle

steps.tx: Physical maturity evaluation focuses on skin texture, sole creases, breast buds, and **external genitalia maturation**. Extremely preterm skin is sticky, gelatinous, and translucent with prominent subcutaneous veins, maturing to parchment-like cracked skin in post-term infants. Plantar creases progress from none at twenty-four weeks, to anterior transverse creases at thirty-two weeks, to full sole creasing at term.
steps.say: Skin maturation, anterior sole creases, and descending testes track physical gestational age.

rows: Faint red marks, anterior crease only
Deep creases across anterior two-thirds of sole
Raised areola with 5 to 10 mm glandular bud
Labia majora completely cover labia minora

steps.tx: Neurological testing assesses increasing passive flexor tone as gestation advances. The **square window wrist angle** measures wrist flexibility by flexing the infant's hand toward the volar forearm. In extremely preterm infants, the angle measures ninety degrees, progressively diminishing to zero degrees in full-term infants due to maturing musculoskeletal tone and ligamentous resistance.
steps.say: The square window angle diminishes from ninety degrees in preterms to zero degrees at full term.

rows: Elbow cannot cross midline of chest

steps.tx: Premature infants face substantial physiological handicaps resulting from **multi-organ system immaturity**. Surfactant deficiency causes respiratory distress syndrome, an immature subependymal germinal matrix predisposes to intraventricular hemorrhage, poor renal tubular concentrating ability impairs fluid balance, and hepatic enzyme immaturity delays bilirubin clearance and drug metabolism, mandating specialized neonatal intensive care.
steps.say: Multi-organ immaturity in preterms causes respiratory failure, intracranial bleeds, and metabolic derangements.

left.title: Critical Organ Vulnerabilities
points: Brain: fragile germinal matrix and IVH risk
Gut: mucosal ischemia and NEC risk

right.title: Metabolic Vulnerabilities
points: Immature immune system and nosocomial sepsis
